archetype.name: Dual-Threat (veteran backup)
archetype.definition: A 12-year veteran who wins on schedule with quick, accurate short throws and designed runs, and who has always paired his mobility with a turnover streak, now serving as Washington's bridge whenever Jayden Daniels sits.

report.headline: Efficient spot duty, inflated by a blowout and a perfect interception line
report.take:
Mariota is Washington's QB2 behind Jayden Daniels, and his season is three uneven cameos rather than a body of work. He played 45% of the snaps in Week 2 at Dallas, every snap in the Week 3 win over Seattle, and only 16% of his lone listed start against Indianapolis. That adds up to 57 dropbacks, so everything below is a hint, not a verdict. Within that sample he has been good. His 0.21 EPA per dropback ranks 11th of 47, his CPOE is 4 points above the league average, and he hasn't thrown an interception or lost a fumble.

The engine is the short game. On throws under 10 air yards he completes 77.8% at 0.248 EPA, and the 0-to-9 band alone is +0.389 with a CPOE of 8.9. His aggressiveness is down to 14.89% from 19.8% last year. He's taking what's there, and Terry McLaurin turned 13 targets into the bulk of his passing value. Two designed runs averaged 22 yards, a reminder that the legs that ranked 6th to 9th in rushing yards at his Tennessee and Atlanta peaks are still there.

The numbers hide where the value came from. In one-score game states he's at -0.014 EPA a play with a 38.1% success rate, roughly league average. Trailing by 9 or more, mostly the Dallas blowout, he's at +0.604 with 75% success against the league's worst defense. Third downs have been poor: -0.276 EPA and a 26.7% conversion rate at 7.4 yards to go. His under-center plays cratered. The deep ball hit only 2 of 8, though both completions were touchdowns. The 7.8% TD rate, 5th in the league, comes from that kind of variance.

The zero-interception line is the most fragile number on the card. He threw 0.78 interceptions a game last season and ranked 54th of 56 in interceptions in 2017. Bet on regression the moment he gets real volume. His role going forward depends entirely on Daniels. And the supporting cast he'd inherit is thinner: McLaurin is on injured reserve after patellar tendon surgery, Jaylin Lane is done, and Laremy Tunsil isn't due back until late December.

strengths.title: Accurate, on-schedule short passing
strengths.body: Most of his value came on throws under 10 air yards, where he completed 77.8% with a CPOE of 7.5. That fits a career built on above-expected accuracy: his 2018 and 2025 CPOE both ranked 13th. This is the most repeatable part of his game, though it leaned heavily on McLaurin, who is now out for the year.

strengths.title: Designed runs still produce chunks
strengths.body: Two designed runs went for 22 yards a carry and +1.768 EPA each. The sample is tiny, but he ranked 13th in rushing yards in just nine games last year. The legs remain the reason Washington can keep a Daniels-style offense intact when he plays.

strengths.title: Avoiding sacks under heavy pressure
strengths.body: He's been pressured on 38.9% of dropbacks, the worst rate of 38 qualifiers, yet only 14.3% of those pressures became sacks, 2nd best. That's a sharp break from a career of bottom-tier pressure-to-sack rates: 49th of 54 in 2018 and 47th of 68 in 2022. Expect it to drift back toward his norm, particularly with Tunsil out.

concerns.title: Value padded by blowout snaps
concerns.body: Trailing by 9 or more, he's at +0.604 EPA a play; in one-score states he's slightly below zero. A good chunk of his efficiency came against prevent looks from Dallas, now the 32nd-ranked defense. In competitive football he has been closer to a replacement-level passer.

concerns.title: Third downs and the clean INT line
concerns.body: He converted just 26.7% of third downs at -0.276 EPA, and the throws beyond the sticks haven't been there: 25% completions on deep shots. The zero interceptions will not hold for a passer who averaged 0.78 a game last season and has ranked in the bottom half in interceptions most years.

concerns.title: Cast eroding around him
concerns.body: McLaurin was his best target by a wide margin and is now on injured reserve. Washington's line already ranks 26th in hit rate allowed, and Tunsil is out. Any future spot start comes with less help than the one he just had.

trend.note: Snap shares of 45%, 100% and 16% tell the story: relief duty, a full game in the Seattle win, then a short start against Indianapolis. He hasn't appeared since Daniels returned in Week 5.

nextGame.headline: Likely holding a clipboard; a brutal draw if he plays
nextGame.body:
He is listed as QB2 and Daniels started Week 8, with no injury designation in the dossier. Barring news, Mariota's role against the Rams is emergency duty. If he does see the field, this defense ranks 4th in EPA and 5th against the pass. It allows the fewest deep EPA in the league and ranks 5th on short throws, which takes away the short game that has carried him. The one opening is that the Rams rarely get home: 29th in hit rate and 27th in sack rate. That would give him time he didn't have against Seattle.

On availability, McLaurin's loss strips his most productive target. On the Rams' side, both starting corners, Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson, are questionable, which would soften the secondary if either sits. Myles Garrett is on track to practice and could juice that weak pass rush. Matthew Stafford's arm soreness matters for game script: the Rams are favored by 5.5, and Washington sits at +195 on the moneyline.

keyMatchups.title: Short game vs a stingy underneath defense
keyMatchups.body: His best work came on throws under 10 yards. The Rams allow -0.098 EPA on short throws, 5th best, and have been the league's best against deep passes. There's no easy area to attack.

keyMatchups.title: Light Rams rush vs his pressure problem
keyMatchups.body: He has faced the highest pressure rate among qualifiers. The Rams' defense ranks 29th in hit rate and 27th in sack rate, so a clean pocket is plausible unless Garrett's return changes the picture.

nextGame.watch: Whether Daniels shows up on the Week 9 injury report; without that, Mariota doesn't take a meaningful snap.

restOfSeason.body:
As long as Daniels is healthy, Mariota is a backup whose weekly line is usually zero, which is why the per-game ranges below sit so low. If he is pressed into a start, expect something like 170-220 passing yards on accurate short throws, a few designed runs, and a real chance of interceptions returning. His career baseline is a roughly league-average passer with good mobility and a turnover habit, not the 0.21 EPA-per-dropback version from 57 dropbacks.

The pieces that should hold are short-area accuracy and rushing value. The pieces that will regress are the 7.8% TD rate, the zero interceptions and the sack avoidance under pressure. Losing McLaurin and Tunsil lowers the ceiling on any spot start.

confidence.note: 57 dropbacks across three erratic appearances, as a backup whose usage depends on another player's health.
